basics.name: Mingxuan Wang
basics.label: B.S. Computer Science and Engineering
basics.summary: A CS undergraduate at CUHK-Shenzhen (SDS), researching spoken language processing and generative AI for (multilingual) speech & audio.

location.address: Longxiang Ave. No. 2001, The Chinese University of Hong Kong Shenzhen

education.institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-Shenzhen)

publications.name: TokenChain: Fully Discrete Machine Speech Chain
publications.summary: Couples semantic-token ASR with a two-stage TTS and uses straight-through estimators for end-to-end feedback; submitted to ICASSP 2026.

publications.name: SingVisio: Visual Analytics of Diffusion Model for Singing Voice Conversion
publications.summary: Defined objective criteria of audio data to visualize diffusion training dynamics; designed and analyzed 20+ expert surveys; co-authored paper and produced a demo video.

publications.name: Amphion: An Open-Source Audio, Music and Speech Generation Toolkit
publications.summary: Contributed to evaluation pipeline for text-to-speech; improved benchmarking efficiency; enhanced large-dataset TTS with multi-speaker functionality.

work.name: CUHK-Shenzhen, Spoken Language Communications (SLC) Lab
work.summary: Independent research under Prof. Satoshi Nakamura on a fully discrete machine speech chain (TokenChain).
highlights: Pioneered the research question and led the end-to-end project: a fully discretized semantic token ASR--TTS machine speech chain with straight-through (STE) / Soft-Gumbel feedback and dynamic loss scheduling.

Demonstrated effectiveness with discrete-token chaining: in-domain beat baseline by 2–6 epochs with 5-13% lower equal-epoch error; out-of-domain cut ASR WER 56% and T2S WER 31% with minimal forgetting.

Drove an independent, first-author effort: engineered a unified preprocess-training-evaluation framework, ablated hyperparameters and produced figures, and submitted the manuscript to IEEE ICASSP 2026.

work.name: Technical University of Munich (TUM)
work.summary: Investigated semantics–syntax separation in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models under Prof. Georg Groh.
highlights: Architected innovative MoE LLM with semantic-syntactic separation mechanism, designed label-aware and adaptive routers with load-balancing and mask, achieving expert-set specialisation with strong results.

Conceived knowledge distillation and compression methods (router-side SLAR; expert-side MoKE) for the new model, delivering 1.2x faster inference and 35% lower memory with only 0.41% performance loss.
Built the full training and evaluation stack with metrics and interpretability tools (routing heatmaps and word banks), ran ablations and authored the poster and research report documenting findings.

work.name: CUHK-Shenzhen, School of Data Science (SDS)
work.summary: Investigated contamination-transfer ablations for multimodal LLMs under Prof. Benyou Wang.
highlights: Proposed novel contamination-transfer ablations investigating unimodal and its derived multimodal models.
Improved key correct-answer matching algorithm for leakage detection, boosting selection accuracy by 20%.

Optimized contamination detection by inhibiting random guessing via uncertainty clause, analyzed back-translation quality through semantic retention and lexical overlap with SBERT, BLEU and their correlation.

work.name: CUHK-Shenzhen, Human Language Technology Lab
work.summary: Conducted research on text-to-speech (TTS) under Prof. Zhizheng Wu.
highlights: Accelerated Amphion & SingVisio's TTS development by optimizing code for critical evaluation milestones.
Implemented Mamba SSM text-to-semantic models attaining higher speaker similarity than Llama baseline.

Developed expertise in two-stage discrete tokenized TTS paradigm, gaining insights into masked-generative text-to-semantic modeling, RVQ-based speech tokenisation, and semantic-to-acoustic synthesis workflows.

work.name: The Hong Kong Research Institute of Textiles and Apparel (HKRITA)
work.summary: Supported enterprise systems and cloud strategy initiatives.
highlights: Managed the ERP system across 20+ projects
Led feasibility study for a cloud-based service adoption
Collaborated with Microsoft and partners on migration planning, cloud architectures, and IT strategy

Men of the year 2014 by Time magazine
